description: Red Oasis is an Omani team building an AI farming advisor that uses NASA satellite data to help farmers save water, with a “Mars mode” for space greenhouses. Join us to build a real prototype. We need Python/ML, web development, or agriculture skills.
summary: Red Oasis is a bilingual (English and Arabic) decision-support web app for date-palm farming at Ad Dariz, Ibri, Oman, where a published study found that palm water demand exceeds falaj supply from April to November. It combines NASA SMAP soil moisture, MODIS/VIIRS vegetation, GPM rainfall and NASA POWER weather with local soil and crop evidence. The app gives an experimental 3-day soil-moisture forecast, a provisional irrigation level (irrigate, monitor or none) with the reasons behind it, a SHAP explanation, a replay of real test days, and a slider where the farmer sets the yield loss they would accept to save water. A Mars tab applies the same water-budget idea to a closed greenhouse as a concept.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Date-palm oases in Oman are watered by aflaj on fixed schedules. A published study of Falaj al-Dariz in Ibri (Al-Ghafri, 2006; observations 2002-2003) found annual palm water demand of 3,620 mm against 3,235 mm supplied: about 10.6% short, with a shortage from April to November and a surplus in winter. Red Oasis turns free NASA Earth observations into an explainable irrigation decision-support tool for this site.

HOW IT WORKS

1. NASA data for the Ad Dariz study point (23.3086 N, 56.6131 E): SMAP soil moisture, MODIS/VIIRS NDVI, GPM IMERG rainfall and NASA POWER weather, from which we calculate FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration (ET0). Suspect rain days, missing satellite passes and NDVI availability lags are handled so the model never uses future information.

2. A Random Forest forecasts SMAP soil moisture 3 days ahead.

3. A provisional four-check rule (soil now, forecast, recent rain vs 3 x ET0, ET0) gives a level: irrigate, monitor or none, with every check shown.

4. SHAP explains how each input moved the forecast.

5. A strategy explorer uses a published Omani trial (Al Kamil and Al Wafi, Khalas palms) so the farmer can set the yield loss they would accept to save water.

6. "Replay a real day" shows what the app would have said on a past test day and what SMAP actually observed 3 days later, using a model trained only on earlier days.

7. A Mars tab applies the same water-budget idea to a closed, water-recycling greenhouse as a labelled concept.

HONEST RESULTS AND LIMITS

On 122 held-out days the model's error was 1.20 percentage points against 1.31 for a "no change" forecast, but in cross-validation it was 1.18 against 1.03, so we label it experimental. A longer 2015-2026 record was tested and did not change this. SMAP covers about 9 km, so the forecast is regional, not field-level. The model does not predict crop stress or yield, and the irrigation levels are not yet validated with field data. Date palm is a perennial crop, so instead of crop rotation we address the challenge's goals of water conservation and adaptation through irrigation decisions.

IMPACT

Farmers, extension officers and researchers get a transparent tool that links satellite data to irrigation timing, shows its reasoning and admits its limits. Next steps: field soil-moisture measurements, grower irrigation logs, palm-specific thresholds and trials with farmers at Ad Dariz.

TOOLS

Python, Streamlit, pandas, scikit-learn, SHAP, Altair; NASA Earthdata AppEEARS, GES DISC and the POWER API; GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud. Interface in English and Arabic.

Live app: https://red-oasis.streamlit.app/

Code: https://github.com/Asmaborghan/red-oasis

USE OF AI TOOLS

The team used AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini) to help write, review and debug code, translate interface text into Arabic, and draft and edit documentation and pitch text. All data come from NASA services, all evaluation numbers are produced by our own code, and the team checked every number and claim.

UPDATES AFTER LOCAL JUDGING

The app is now a dashboard with tabs (Advisor, Model performance, Site and evidence, Challenge and data, Earth and Mars, Next steps and limits), with Arabic chart versions. Automatic data quality checks were added (python -m model.data_quality): date gaps, duplicates, physical ranges, filled values and suspect rain; the current file shows no failures.

FUTURE PLAN (not yet built)

Phase 1 (3 months): validate the forecast with soil sensors and farmer irrigation logs at Ad Dariz, run the data checks before every retraining, test rain forecasts as a model input, and simplify the interface further.

Phase 2 (6 months): a daily agent that fetches the latest NASA data and forecasts the coming days; SMS or WhatsApp alerts, sent only after the forecast is compared with field data; trials with farmers and extension officers in Ad Dariz.

Phase 3 (1 year): a mobile app with alerts, then seasonal crops, which would open the door to crop rotation.

Details: https://github.com/Asmaborghan/red-oasis/blob/main/FUTURE_PLAN.md
